header.userPrompt:
Add duplicate-expense detection to the expenses page plus a backend merge operation, so the user can find and collapse expenses that represent the same purchase (one linked to a bank statement row, the other linked to a receipt).

## Background: the real problem
The user imported two years of CARREFOUR receipts (each became an expense linked to its receipt) AFTER importing "Ready" bank statement rows that rules had matched to CARREFOUR (each became an expense linked to its row). The result is duplicate expense pairs: for one real purchase there are now two expenses, one carrying the bank statement row, the other carrying the receipt. They want to detect such pairs and merge each into a single expense that keeps the row and gains the receipt. This is a one-time-shaped cleanup but must generalize to any merchant, not just CARREFOUR.

Note: the recently shipped Ready-tab receipt auto-match only attaches receipts that are still UNLINKED at process time. These duplicates already both became expenses, so that feature does not fix them. This is a separate detect-and-merge flow.

## Scope decision: phase 1, frontend detection + backend merge, NO persistence
- Detection runs in the frontend. The expenses page already loads all expenses; compute duplicate candidates client-side. Do NOT add a detection endpoint, a suggestions table, or any persisted "dismiss/ignore" state in this phase. Dismissing a suggestion is in-memory only (it reappears on reload); this is intentional so we can first measure how many real duplicates and how many false candidates exist before deciding whether a persisted inbox is worth building. Do not build that inbox now.
- Merge runs in the backend as one transaction (details below).

## Detection (frontend, pure + unit-tested)
Add a pure function (natural home: a new object under `net.wiringbits.utils` or alongside the expenses-page logic, matching how other pages keep pure logic in a `*Logic`/util object) that takes the loaded expenses and returns duplicate candidates. A candidate is a PAIR of two expenses where:
- exactly one of the two has a bank_statement_row linked and the other has NO row linked (survivor = the row-linked one, loser = the no-row one);
- the two amounts are equal (exact, same currency/sign handling as the rest of the app; do not fabricate or coerce);
- the two dates are equal, or within the same small day window already used by the matcher (reuse `ReconciliationMatcher.MaxDateDifferenceDays` rather than a new constant). A missing date is never a match.

Tier the candidates by confidence:
- STRONG: amount + date + MERCHANT all match (same merchant id). High confidence, one-click merge.
- WEAK: amount + date match but MERCHANT differs. Lower confidence, shown separately, user must view the receipt to compare before merging.

Explicit exclusions (must be unit-tested):
- two expenses with the same amount+date(+merchant) but BOTH linked to rows (to different rows) are NOT candidates, they are two real transactions;
- a pair where NEITHER has a row is out of scope (no row-survivor), not a candidate;
- a missing date on either side is never a candidate.

## Merge (backend, one transaction)
New action + endpoint to merge a loser expense into a survivor expense, both owned by the authenticated user (user-scoped checks on every query). Given survivorId and loserId:
1. validate both belong to the user and that the survivor has a row linked and the loser does not (reject otherwise, loud error, no silent no-op);
2. repoint the loser's receipt link to the survivor (reuse the existing receipt link path / `receiptRepository.linkToExpense` and its unlinked-only guard semantics; the survivor must not already have a receipt, else fail loudly);
3. repoint any `refund` rows that reference the loser (`refund.expense_id`) to the survivor. This matters: `refund.expense_id` is `ON DELETE SET NULL`, so a plain delete would silently orphan a refund. Carry it over instead;
4. delete the loser expense. Its `expense_category_split` rows are `ON DELETE CASCADE` and go away with it (the survivor keeps its own splits, which is the intended outcome);
5. all of the above in a single DB transaction.

Confirm against the schema (evolutions) that these are the only FKs referencing `expense(id)`: `expense_category_split` (CASCADE), `bank_statement_row.expense_id` (SET NULL), `receipt.expense_id` (SET NULL), `refund.expense_id` (SET NULL). If a new reference exists, handle it; do not leave a silently-nulled reference.

The survivor keeps its own amount, date, merchant, category, splits, and row link. The loser contributes only its receipt (and any refund). The merge never changes the survivor's own fields.

## UI (expenses page)
- Surface duplicate candidates on the expenses page (a section, tab, or panel consistent with the existing page structure). Show STRONG and WEAK groups separately.
- Each candidate shows the two expenses side by side: amount, date, merchant, category, which side has the row vs the receipt, so the user can compare.
- Provide a way to VIEW the receipt to compare before merging. Reuse the existing shared receipt-file viewer helper `net.wiringbits.utils.ReceiptFileViewer` (added in the previous PR, opens the receipt file in a new tab). Do NOT duplicate blob/Uint8Array open logic and do NOT build a new modal.
- The user decides per pair: "Merge" (calls the backend merge, survivor = the row-linked expense) or "Dismiss" (in-memory hide for this session only; no persistence).
- After a successful merge, update the page state in place (the loser disappears, the survivor now shows the receipt) following the existing page-scoped state pattern; do not force a full remount/refetch if the page already avoids that.

## Rules and constraints
- Merge is destructive (deletes an expense). It is always explicit per pair and user-confirmed. Never auto-merge, never bulk-merge in this phase.
- Survivor is ALWAYS the row-linked expense; loser is ALWAYS the no-row expense. Reject any merge request that does not fit this shape.
- No silent bad data: exact amount match, never a fabricated date, fail loudly on any guard violation (loser has no receipt, survivor already has a receipt, either not owned by user, wrong row/no-row shape).
- All DB queries user-scoped (WHERE user_id = ?); list queries have a stable ORDER BY.
- No DB CHECK constraints for business rules; app-level validation.
- Follow `docs/guide/frontend.md` and `docs/guide/testing.md`. Test descriptions name a single method (no type prefix), per `.orca/reviewers/tests.md`.
- Match existing code style; surgical changes only.

## Tests
- Frontend detection: unit-test STRONG vs WEAK tiering, exact-amount requirement, date-window boundaries (0, MaxDateDifferenceDays, just outside), missing-date excluded, both-rows excluded, neither-row excluded, correct survivor/loser assignment.
- Backend merge: receipt relinked to survivor, refund rows repointed to survivor, loser deleted, loser's splits gone, survivor's own fields unchanged, all in one transaction; guard failures (not owned, wrong shape, survivor already has a receipt) rejected. Follow the existing action/repository test patterns.
- Full suite must pass as CI runs it.

## Out of scope (do NOT build now)
- No persisted suggestions/inbox table, no persisted dismiss/ignore state.
- No detection endpoint (detection is frontend-only).
- No auto-merge or bulk-merge.
- No changes to the Ready-tab receipt auto-match, the Auto-Reconcile page, or `ReconciliationMatcher.reconcile`.
- No new receipt-view modal (reuse `ReceiptFileViewer`).
- No change to how receipts or rows are parsed, imported, or confirmed.

resultJson.description:
Importing CARREFOUR receipts after the matching bank statement rows had already become expenses left duplicate pairs. For a single purchase there is one expense linked to a `bank_statement_row` and a second expense linked to a `receipt`. This epic lets the user find those pairs on the Expenses page and collapse each one into the row-linked expense. That expense keeps all of its own fields, splits and row link, and gains the receipt. It works for any merchant, not only CARREFOUR. Detection is client-side only: a pure function runs over the already-loaded `GetExpenses` data. A pair qualifies when exactly one side has a row, the amounts are exactly equal, and the dates are within `ReconciliationMatcher.MaxDateDifferenceDays`. Pairs are tiered STRONG (same merchant id) or WEAK (merchant differs). There is no detection endpoint, no suggestions table and no persisted dismiss state. Dismiss lasts only for the session, by design, so we can first measure how many real duplicates and false candidates there are.

The merge is a new user-scoped backend operation that runs in one DB transaction. It validates the shape: both expenses are owned by the user, the survivor has a row, the loser has no row, the loser has a receipt, and the survivor has no receipt. Then it moves the loser's receipt to the survivor through the existing unlinked-only `ReceiptDAO.setExpenseId` guard, moves any `refund.expense_id` that points at the loser over to the survivor, and deletes the loser (its splits cascade). Every guard violation fails loudly with a `RuntimeException`. The schema has exactly four FKs to `expense(id)`, all in evolution 3.sql: `expense_category_split` (CASCADE), `refund` (SET NULL), `bank_statement_row` (SET NULL) and `receipt` (SET NULL). Evolution 12.sql adds partial unique indexes on `receipt(expense_id)` and `bank_statement_row(expense_id)`. The loser has no row by definition, and its receipt and refunds are moved explicitly, so nothing is silently nulled.

The UI adds a duplicates section to the Expenses page. STRONG and WEAK groups are shown separately, with the two expenses side by side, a receipt "View" button that reuses `ReceiptFileViewer.openInNewTab`, and per-pair Merge (with a confirm dialog) and Dismiss. After a merge, page-local state is patched in place, the same way `deletedIds` already works for deletes: the loser disappears and the survivor shows the receipt. There is no refetch or remount. One assumption beyond the literal spec: detection also requires `loser.receiptIds.nonEmpty && survivor.receiptIds.isEmpty`, because the backend rejects any other pair and showing pairs that can never merge would be noise. A side effect is that recomputing after a merge drops any other pairs that involved the merged expenses.

tasks.title: Frontend pure duplicate detection (ExpenseDuplicateDetector) + unit tests
tasks.description:
Create `web/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/utils/ExpenseDuplicateDetector.scala`, a pure object in the same style as `ReconciliationMatcher`. Suggested API: `enum Tier { case Strong, Weak }`, `case class Candidate(survivor: GetExpenses.Response.Expense, loser: GetExpenses.Response.Expense, tier: Tier)`, and `def detect(expenses: List[GetExpenses.Response.Expense]): List[Candidate]`.

Rules:
- survivor = the expense with `rowIds.nonEmpty`; loser = the expense with `rowIds.isEmpty`. Pairs where both or neither side has a row are excluded.
- loser must have `receiptIds.nonEmpty` and survivor must have `receiptIds.isEmpty` (mirrors the merge guards; document this in the scaladoc).
- `survivor.amount == loser.amount`: exact BigDecimal value equality, no abs, no tolerance.
- `Math.abs(survivor.date.toEpochDay - loser.date.toEpochDay) <= ReconciliationMatcher.MaxDateDifferenceDays`. Use the symmetric window, as `reconcile` does. Reuse the constant; do not add a new one.
- Strong when both `merchantId`s are defined and equal; otherwise Weak (`None`/`None` counts as Weak).
- Avoid O(n²) over two years of data: group losers by amount, then check the date window.
- Return a stable order, e.g. survivor date desc, then survivor id, then loser id.

`GetExpenses.Response.Expense.date` is a non-optional `LocalDate`, so a missing date cannot be represented. State this in the scaladoc as the guarantee behind "a missing date never matches". Do not change the model, and do not add a test that cannot be constructed.

Tests go in `web/src/test/scala/net/wiringbits/utils/ExpenseDuplicateDetectorSpec.scala` (AnyWordSpec, `"detect" should { ... }`, no type prefix in descriptions). Cover: Strong vs Weak tiering (including both merchants None → Weak); exact amount required (10.00 vs 10.01 → none); date diff 0, == MaxDateDifferenceDays, and MaxDateDifferenceDays+1 (excluded), in both directions; both-rows excluded; neither-row excluded; survivor/loser assignment regardless of input order; loser without a receipt excluded; survivor that already has a receipt excluded. Verify with `sbt "web/testOnly *ExpenseDuplicateDetectorSpec"` (Node 24 must be on PATH).

tasks.title: Backend merge in one transaction: DAO helpers + ExpensesRepository.merge + repository tests
tasks.description:
Add the reusable queries to the DAOs (user-scoped; any list query gets a stable ORDER BY):
- `ReceiptDAO.findByExpenseId(expenseId: UUID, userId: UUID): Option[Receipt]`, using the same SELECT/JOIN as `find`, with `WHERE r.expense_id = ? AND r.user_id = ?`. At most one row exists because of `receipt_expense_id_unique`.
- `BankStatementRowDAO.existsForExpense(expenseId: UUID, userId: UUID): Boolean`. Scope it with `bank_statement_id IN (SELECT id FROM bank_statement WHERE user_id = ?)`, as `setExpenseIdForUser` does; `bank_statement_row` has no user_id column.
- `RefundDAO.reassignExpense(fromExpenseId: UUID, toExpenseId: UUID, userId: UUID, updatedAt: Instant): Int` (UPDATE refund SET expense_id = to, updated_at WHERE expense_id = from AND user_id = ?). Zero rows is valid.

Add `ExpensesRepository.merge(survivorId: UUID, loserId: UUID, userId: UUID): Future[Unit]`. Run it under `database.withTransaction`, wrapped in `ConstraintViolations.translating(ReceiptRepository.ReceiptExpenseIdUnique)`. Steps, in order, each failing with a distinct `RuntimeException` message:
1. Reject `survivorId == loserId`.
2. `ExpenseDAO.find(survivorId, userId)` and `ExpenseDAO.find(loserId, userId)`, otherwise "Expense not found". This covers the not-owned case.
3. The survivor must have a row (`existsForExpense`) and the loser must not.
4. The loser must have a receipt (`findByExpenseId`), and the survivor must not have one.
5. `ReceiptDAO.clearExpenseId(receipt.id, userId, now)`, then `ReceiptDAO.setExpenseId(receipt.id, userId, survivorId, now)`. Reuse the unlinked-only guard; do not call `ReceiptRepository.linkToExpense`, because it opens its own transaction.
6. `RefundDAO.reassignExpense(loserId, survivorId, userId, now)`.
7. `ExpenseDAO.delete(loserId, userId)` (splits cascade).

Use `clock.instant()` for `now`. Never touch the survivor's own columns or its splits.

Tests go in `server/src/test/scala/net/wiringbits/repositories/ExpensesRepositorySpec.scala` under `"merge" should`. Use `RepositoryUtils` (`createUser`, `createExpense`, `createReceipt`, `createRefund`, `createCategory`, `createMerchant`) and the spec's existing `linkToNewRow(userId, expenseId)` helper. Link a receipt with `repositories.receipts.linkToExpense`. No raw SQL seeding. Cases: the receipt now points at the survivor (`receipts.find(...).expenseId`); refunds that pointed at the loser now point at the survivor; the loser is deleted and its splits are gone while the survivor's splits remain; the survivor's amount, date, merchantId, notes and row link are unchanged. Rejection cases: another user's expense; survivor without a row; loser with a row; loser without a receipt; survivor that already has a receipt; same id twice. For a rejection after a partial step (survivor already has a receipt), assert nothing changed: the loser still exists and its receipt is still linked to it. Verify with `sbt "server/testOnly *ExpensesRepositorySpec"`.

tasks.title: Merge endpoint: shared Tapir model/endpoint, action, controller, ApiClient + controller tests
tasks.description:
Shared API (`lib/api/shared/`):
- Add `net.wiringbits.api.models.expenses.MergeExpenses` with `case class Request(loserId: UUID)` and `case class Response()`. Give both Play JSON `Format` and Tapir `Schema` with unique `SName`s (`MergeExpensesRequest`/`MergeExpensesResponse`), following `DeleteExpense.scala`/`UpdateExpense.scala`.
- Add `ExpensesEndpoints.merge`: `baseEndpoint.post.in(path[UUID]("expenseId")).in("merge").in(jsonBody[MergeExpenses.Request]).in(userAuth).out(jsonBody[MergeExpenses.Response]).errorOut(oneOf(HttpErrors.badRequest))`, with summary "Merge a duplicate expense (loser) into a bank-row-linked expense (survivor)". Add it to `routes`. The path id is the survivor.
- Add `ApiClient.mergeExpenses(survivorId: UUID, request: MergeExpenses.Request): Future[MergeExpenses.Response]` via `handleRequest(ExpensesEndpoints.merge, (survivorId, request, dummyUserId))`.

Server:
- Add `server/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/actions/expenses/MergeExpensesAction.scala` as a thin action (`@Inject() (expensesRepository: ExpensesRepository)(implicit ec)`) whose `apply(survivorId, loserId, userId)` calls `expensesRepository.merge` and returns `MergeExpenses.Response()`.
- Wire it into `controllers/ExpensesController.scala` as a `merge` handler modeled on `delete`, using `handleRequest` and `logger.info(s"Merge expense $loserId into $survivorId")`, and register `ExpensesEndpoints.merge.serverLogic(merge)` in `routes`.

Tests go in `server/src/test/scala/controllers/ExpensesControllerSpec.scala` under `"POST /expenses/:id/merge" should`. Happy path: create two expenses through the client, link one to a row with `createBankStatementWithRows` + `client.linkRowToExpense` (see the existing unlinkedOnly test), link a receipt to the other, merge, then check that `client.getExpenses` returns only the survivor with `receiptIds` = the receipt and `rowIds` = the row. Errors: another user's survivor or loser fails (use `buildClient()` + a second `createVerifyLoginUser`); swapped shape (row-linked expense as loser) fails. Check how other controller specs create and link receipts to choose the receipt setup; prefer the repository/injector path that `PlayPostgresSpec` exposes over raw SQL. Fix any test-side `ApiClient` subclasses that fail to compile. Verify with `CI=true sbt Test/compile` and `sbt "server/testOnly *ExpensesControllerSpec"`.

tasks.title: Expenses page duplicates section: STRONG/WEAK groups, view receipt, merge (confirmed) and session-only dismiss, in-place state update
tasks.description:
Pure state helpers go in the `ExpenseList` object in `web/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/components/pages/expenses/ExpensesPage.scala`, next to `applyDeletedIds`. Add `applyMerges(expenses: List[GetExpenses.Response.Expense], merges: Map[UUID, UUID]): List[...]`, where the map is survivorId → receiptId; it adds the receipt id to the survivor's `receiptIds`. The losers are already removed by `deletedIds`. Also add a dismiss key helper, e.g. `dismissKey(c: Candidate): String = s"${c.survivor.id}:${c.loser.id}"`. Unit-test `applyMerges` in `web/src/test/scala/net/wiringbits/components/pages/expenses/ExpensesPageSpec.scala` (`"applyMerges" should ...`).

State in `ExpenseList.component`:
- `val (mergedReceipts, setMergedReceipts) = Hooks.useState[Map[UUID, UUID]](Map.empty)`
- `val (dismissed, setDismissed) = Hooks.useState[Set[String]](Set.empty)`, in memory only.
- `pendingMerge: Option[Candidate]` for the confirm dialog.
- `showDuplicates: Boolean`.

Run detection on ALL loaded expenses: `applyMerges(applyDeletedIds(sortedExpenses, deletedIds), mergedReceipts)`, not the date- or text-filtered list. Memoize it with `SafeHooks.useMemo(key)` where the key is a String built from expense count, `deletedIds` and `mergedReceipts`; never pass collections as deps. Filter out dismissed keys. Feed the same merged list into the existing `visibleExpenses` pipeline so the main list's receipt cell reflects the merge. On merge confirm, call `props.ctx.api.client.mergeExpenses(c.survivor.id, MergeExpenses.Request(c.loser.id)).onComplete`. On `Success`, run `setDeletedIds(deletedIds + c.loser.id)` and `setMergedReceipts(mergedReceipts + (c.survivor.id -> c.loser.receiptIds.head))`. On `Failure`, `setError(ex.getMessage)`. Do not call `props.onRefresh()`, which would refetch and remount.

Rendering: put the panel in a new file, `web/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/components/pages/expenses/ExpenseDuplicatesPanel.scala`, using the RULE-FE-001 shape. Props: ctx, candidates, categories, onMerge(Candidate), onDismiss(Candidate), onError(String).
- Show separate STRONG and WEAK headed groups with counts. Explain that WEAK means the merchant differs and the user should check the receipt first.
- Each candidate is a two-column side-by-side card for survivor ("Bank row") and loser ("Receipt"): amount (`ExpenseList.formatAmount`), date, merchantName or "—", first category name from splits.
- Buttons: "View receipt", "Merge" and "Dismiss".
- "View receipt" calls `ReceiptFileViewer.openInNewTab(props.ctx.api.client, receiptId, filename, props.onError)`. It needs the filename, so the panel loads `getReceipts` once with `AsyncComponent` (it mounts only when the section is shown) and looks up `documentFilename` by id. Do not use the `/api/receipts/{id}/file` URL path, and add no new modal or blob code.
- Every mapped element needs `.withKey`, and object-level vals hold only CSS literals.

Entry point: when candidates are non-empty, add a toolbar button such as "Possible duplicates (N)" that toggles `showDuplicates`. Render the panel between `errorMsg` and `expenseList`.

Merge confirmation: add an `mui.Dialog` modeled on `deleteDialog`, saying the receipt moves to the bank-row expense and the receipt-only expense is deleted, with buttons Cancel and Merge (color error). Never auto-merge or bulk-merge.

No DOM test unless it guards a known crash (RULE-TE-010). Do not modify the existing receipt cell in the expense rows. Verify with `CI=true sbt Test/compile` and `sbt "web/testOnly *ExpensesPageSpec *ExpenseDuplicateDetectorSpec"`.

resultJson.brief:
## Layout
- `lib/api/shared/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/api/`: Tapir endpoints (`endpoints/ExpensesEndpoints.scala`), request/response models (`models/expenses/*.scala`), and `ApiClient.scala`, which both the frontend and the controller tests use. New endpoints MUST go here.
- `server/`: Play backend. Flow is controller (`server/src/main/scala/controllers/ExpensesController.scala`) → thin action (`net/wiringbits/actions/expenses/*Action.scala`) → repository (`net/wiringbits/repositories/ExpensesRepository.scala`) → DAO (`repositories/daos/*DAO.scala`, Anorm SQL interpolation).
- `web/`: Scala.js + Slinky + MUI 5.
  - Expenses page: `web/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/components/pages/expenses/ExpensesPage.scala`. It contains `ExpensesPage` (three nested `AsyncComponent` fetches: expenses, merchants, categories) and `ExpenseList` (the real component and its pure helpers).
  - Pure utils live in `web/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/utils/` (`ReconciliationMatcher.scala`, `ReceiptFileViewer.scala`).
- Evolutions: `server/src/main/resources/evolutions/default/*.sql`.
  - 3.sql defines the FKs to `expense(id)`: `expense_category_split` ON DELETE CASCADE; `refund.expense_id`, `bank_statement_row.expense_id` and `receipt.expense_id` ON DELETE SET NULL.
  - 12.sql adds the partial unique indexes `receipt_expense_id_unique` and `bank_statement_row_expense_id_unique`.
  - No other references exist. No new evolution is needed.

## Key types and APIs
- `GetExpenses.Response.Expense(id, amount: BigDecimal, date: LocalDate /*non-optional*/, time, merchantId: Option[UUID], merchantName: Option[String], notes, splits: List[Split(id, categoryId, amount)], createdAt, receiptIds: List[UUID] = Nil, rowIds: List[UUID] = Nil)`. `GetExpensesAction` fills `receiptIds`/`rowIds` from receipts and rows. Row-created expenses store positive amounts (`row.amount.abs`).
- `ReconciliationMatcher.MaxDateDifferenceDays = 3L`. `reconcile` uses the symmetric `Math.abs(a.toEpochDay - b.toEpochDay) <= MaxDateDifferenceDays`. Do NOT modify `ReconciliationMatcher`.
- `ReceiptFileViewer.openInNewTab(client: ApiClient, receiptId: UUID, filename: String, onError: String => Unit)(using ExecutionContext): Unit`. It opens the tab synchronously (popup-safe) and needs the filename for the MIME type. Filenames come from `client.getReceipts: Future[GetReceipts.Response]` (`Receipt.documentFilename`, `Receipt.expenseId`).
- Repository/DAO:
  - `ExpensesRepository(database: Database)(implicit ec: DatabaseExecutionContext, clock: Clock)`. Methods wrap `database.withConnection` / `withTransaction { implicit conn => ... }` in a `Future`.
  - `ExpenseDAO.find(id, userId): Option[Expense]` and `ExpenseDAO.delete(id, userId)` (throws "Expense not found" when 0 rows).
  - `ReceiptDAO.setExpenseId(id, userId, expenseId, updatedAt)` only updates when `expense_id IS NULL`, else throws "Receipt already linked to an expense". `ReceiptDAO.clearExpenseId(id, userId, updatedAt)`.
  - `ReceiptRepository.linkToExpense` opens its OWN transaction, so it cannot be composed inside another one. Compose the DAO calls instead.
  - `ReceiptRepository.ReceiptExpenseIdUnique` holds the constraint-name→message pair used with `ConstraintViolations.translating(...)(block)`.
  - `RefundDAO.setExpenseId` only works for unlinked refunds (not suitable for repointing). `RefundDAO.clearExpenseId`.
  - `bank_statement_row` has no `user_id`. Scope it via `bank_statement_id IN (SELECT id FROM bank_statement WHERE user_id = ?)`, as `BankStatementRowDAO.setExpenseIdForUser` does.
- Controller pattern: `private def x(..., userIdF: Future[UUID]): Future[Either[ErrorResponse, R]] = handleRequest { for { userId <- userIdF; r <- action(...) } yield Right(r) }`, registered with `Endpoints.x.serverLogic(x)` in `routes`. A `RuntimeException` message surfaces as a bad-request error.
- Endpoint pattern: `baseEndpoint.post.in(path[UUID](\"expenseId\")).in(\"merge\").in(jsonBody[Req]).in(userAuth).out(jsonBody[Resp]).errorOut(oneOf(HttpErrors.badRequest)).summary(...)`. Models carry Play `Format` plus a Tapir `Schema` with a unique `Schema.SName`.

## Frontend conventions (docs/guide/frontend.md)
- Component shape: `object X { def apply(...): KeyAddingStage = component(Props(...)); case class Props(...); val component = FunctionalComponent[Props] { ... } }`. Pass `AppContext` through Props; no `useContext`.
- Object-level `val`s hold only CSS literals (`new CSSPropertiesUtils { ... }`), never `ReactElement`/`KeyAddingStage`. Use `def` for elements rendered twice. Every mapped element needs `.withKey`.
- Optional rendering: `.fold[ReactElement](Fragment())(...)`.
- Hooks with dependencies use `SafeHooks.useMemo(key: String)` / `SafeHooks.useEffect(key)`. Keys must be Strings; never pass collections, UUIDs or BigDecimals as deps.
- API side effects use `.onComplete { case Success(_) => ...; case Failure(ex) => setError(ex.getMessage) }`.
- No `js.Dynamic`/`asInstanceOf` in pages; keep that interop in `utils`/compat.
- `ExpenseList` already patches state in place for deletes: `deletedIds` plus `applyDeletedIds` and no refetch. Create and update call `props.onRefresh()`, which refetches and remounts; merge must NOT do that.
- `ExpenseList` already has `error`/`setError`, a `deleteDialog` built with `mui.Dialog`/`DialogTitle`/`DialogContent`/`DialogActions` to copy for the confirm, and a toolbar `mui.Box` with buttons.
- Leave the existing row `receiptCell` (`dom.window.open(\"/api/receipts/.../file\")`) untouched; it is out of scope.

## Testing conventions (docs/guide/testing.md, .orca/reviewers/tests.md)
- ScalaTest `AnyWordSpec`, `must` matchers. `should` subjects name only the method or scenario (e.g. `\"merge\" should`, `\"detect\" should`), never the class or object name.
- Repository specs extend `RepositorySpec with RepositoryUtils` and use `withRepositories() { implicit repositories => ... }`. Seed data only via `RepositoryUtils` (`createUser`, `createExpense(userId, amount, date, merchantId, notes, splits)`, `createReceipt(userId)` (filename \"receipt.pdf\"), `createRefund(userId, ..., expenseId = Some(...))`, `createCategory`, `createMerchant`, `createBankStatement`). Never seed with raw SQL.
- `ExpensesRepositorySpec` has a private `linkToNewRow(userId, expenseId)` helper. Failures surface as `intercept[RuntimeException](f.futureValue)` with `ex.getCause.getMessage must include(\"...\")`. Splits: `repositories.expenses.allSplits(userId)` / `findSplitsByExpenseId`.

- Actions are not tested directly; controller tests cover them.
- Frontend: plain unit tests on pure functions (e.g. `ExpensesPageSpec` tests `ExpenseList.sortExpenses`/`applyDeletedIds`; it has an `expense(...)` builder). Add DOM tests only to guard a known crash.
- Targeted runs only: `sbt \"server/testOnly *XSpec\"`, `sbt \"web/testOnly *XSpec\"`, `CI=true sbt Test/compile` (`-Werror`). Web tests need Node 24 on PATH (the default node is v16). Do not run the full `sbt test`.
- Run `sbt scalafmtAll scalafmtSbt` before finishing.

## Rules to remember
- Every query is user-scoped. Do multi-step writes in a single `withTransaction`. Translate unique-index violations by constraint name in the repository. Fail loudly; no silent no-ops. No DB CHECK constraints.
- The survivor is always the row-linked expense and is never modified; the loser is always the no-row expense, and must have a receipt.
- Out of scope: no detection endpoint, no persistence of suggestions or dismissals, no auto- or bulk-merge, no changes to the Ready-tab auto-match, the Auto-Reconcile page or `ReconciliationMatcher`.

resultJson.title: Add duplicate-expense detection and merge to the expenses page
resultJson.body:
Importing CARREFOUR receipts after the matching bank statement rows had already become expenses left duplicate pairs: one purchase ends up as two expenses, one linked to the row and one linked to the receipt. This PR lets the user find those pairs on the Expenses page and merge each one into the row-linked expense. It works for any merchant.

- **Detection (frontend only):** `ExpenseDuplicateDetector` runs over the expenses the page has already loaded. A pair qualifies when exactly one side has a row, the loser has a receipt and the survivor has none, the amounts are exactly equal, and the dates are within `ReconciliationMatcher.MaxDateDifferenceDays`. Pairs are STRONG when the merchant id matches and WEAK otherwise. When an expense appears in more than one pair, those pairs are flagged as ambiguous.
- **Merge (backend):** new endpoint `POST /expenses/:survivorId/merge`, which calls `MergeExpensesAction` and then `ExpensesRepository.merge`. In one transaction it checks ownership and the row/receipt shape, moves the loser's receipt to the survivor, moves the loser's refunds to the survivor, and deletes the loser (its splits are deleted with it by cascade). The survivor's own fields are not changed. Every guard failure raises an error with a specific message.
- **UI:** a "Possible duplicates (N)" toolbar button opens a panel with the STRONG and WEAK groups. Each pair is shown side by side with "View receipt" (through `ReceiptFileViewer`), "Merge" (asks for confirmation first) and "Dismiss". After a merge the page state is updated in place, without a refetch.

Notes for reviewers:
- Dismiss lasts only for the current session. There is no detection endpoint and nothing is persisted, by design, so we can first measure how many real and false candidates there are.
- I checked the evolutions: `expense_category_split` (CASCADE) and the SET NULL FKs on `refund`, `receipt` and `bank_statement_row` are the only references to `expense(id)`. The loser has no row by definition, and its receipt and refunds are moved explicitly, so no reference gets silently set to null.
- One addition beyond the spec: detection also requires the loser to have a receipt and the survivor to have none, because the backend rejects every other pair.
- Not tested: rollback when a step fails partway through the merge. It can't be set up deterministically without raw SQL seeding, which the test suite doesn't allow. Atomicity relies on `withTransaction`.
